meta.description: Hand-checkable answer key for the synthetic GC/CM agreement. Used to score the rules extractor (Demo 1).
meta.status: DRAFT: a teammate should read the contract and confirm each entry before scoring.
meta.core_definition: Core rules govern notice, response times, deadlines, pricing, fees, markups, equipment, change authority, payment, claims, and audit. Peripheral rules cover insurance, bonds, termination, dispute mechanics, and meeting cadence.

pitfalls.name: Similar clocks, different triggers
pitfalls.note: Several rules use the same number of days but start from different events. An extractor must record the trigger, not just the number. The 21-day CM-initiated CP (6.3) versus the 14-day Proposal Request CP (6.3, Exhibit E) is the main trap.

pitfalls.name: Rules split across documents
pitfalls.note: The CP deadline appears in Article 6 and Exhibit E; Equipment rules appear in 6.5.4 and Exhibit B; approval authority appears in 6.7 and Exhibit D. A match to either location counts.

pitfalls.name: Exceptions to the Fee
pitfalls.note: The 5% Fee applies to changes (6.5.3) except NSS, SGC adjustments, bond and insurance premiums, B&O taxes, and permit fees. An extractor that reports only the 5% misses the exception. These are the categories closest to the Webster audit findings.

pitfalls.name: Non-rules that look like rules
pitfalls.note: Meeting minutes are not notice (7.7), an RFI response does not authorize cost (7.4), and silence is not acceptance (6.4). These are negative rules. The extractor should not report them as notice windows or approvals.

pitfalls.name: Precedence
pitfalls.note: Exhibit E cannot shorten a notice period or lengthen a response time in the Articles (1.2). If an extractor reports a shorter or longer period from Exhibit E, it should flag the conflict.

pitfalls.name: Cross-references
pitfalls.note: Several rules depend on another section (6.5.5 refers to 5.5; 8.3 and 6.8 refer to 6.2(a); 6.5.6 refers to 5.2). Rules that only cross-reference should still be extracted with the target section.

pitfalls.name: Amounts that are facts, not rules
pitfalls.note: Exhibit A, B, and C line items are budget amounts, not rules. They are not in the key. Amounts that act as limits or rates (for example $3,185 per day, $350 per RFI, $250,000 approval limit) are in the key.

scoring.unit: One rule per entry. A predicted rule matches a key entry when it cites one of the entry's sections, has the same type group, and carries the same value (numbers and units must match exactly; rules with no value match on section and meaning).
scoring.recall: matched key rules / key rules, reported for core rules and for all rules (claim 1 target: at least 85% of core rules).
scoring.citation_validity: share of predicted quotes that appear verbatim (after whitespace and punctuation normalization) in the contract text.
scoring.note: Type labels are a guide. When a predicted rule and a key rule describe the same requirement with a different type label, count it as a match and record the label difference separately.
